dataset.name: PromptToolHub 300 Hero V9.0 Execution-Ready
dataset.rewrite_objective: Replace template-heavy meta-prompts with directly executable, professional, category-native instructions.
major_upgrades: direct execution instead of prompt-generation scaffolding
real category-native deliverables for all 16 top-level categories
subcategory-specific professional workflows and acceptance tests
metric targets treated as hypotheses rather than guaranteed outcomes
explicit output formats and handoff criteria
failure prevention tied to actual task risks
minimal-variable revision after failed acceptance checks
execution-based QA sampling across every top-level category
removed_failure_patterns: generic visual production language applied to non-visual work
repeated placeholder fields that shift work back to the user
generic professional-visual-asset jobs for coding, business, writing, and strategy prompts
platform labels that do not match the task
QA that checks structure instead of whether the task can succeed
success claims implied by target metrics
dataset.architecture: Brief → Inputs/Source of Truth → Category-Native Execution → Deliverable → Acceptance Tests → Minimal Revision

qa_method.coverage: 2 rewritten prompts sampled from each of the 16 top-level categories (32 samples total)
qa_method.test: For each sample, simulate a first execution against a concrete professional fixture and verify that the prompt produces the intended kind of work product, contains enough task-specific direction to act, and has acceptance checks that would catch a bad result.
qa_method.not_a_structural_rewrite: QA focuses on usefulness and correctness of the expected work product, not on whether the prompt has a preferred section count.
qa_method.limitation: This QA is model-simulated within the rewrite pass; no external generation runtime or third-party model API was invoked.

prompts.title: Logo Design - Minimalist AI Unicorn Monogram for Billion-Dollar Brand
prompts.prompt_content:
EXECUTION-READY PROMPT

TASK
You are the brand identity designer. The assignment is: Logo Design - Minimalist AI Unicorn Monogram for Billion-Dollar Brand.
Primary professional job: a distinctive identity asset.
Primary outcome: Minimalist AI Unicorn Monogram for Billion-Dollar Brand.
Use the stated objective (Minimalist AI Unicorn Monogram for Billion-Dollar Brand) as the primary success criterion. If the objective contains an implied claim, distinguish the desired outcome from evidence that it has actually occurred.

INPUTS AND SOURCE OF TRUTH
Use these inputs when supplied: brand/product/reference images, exact copy, dimensions, and any supplied visual references. If a critical input is absent, make the minimum reasonable assumption and label it; do not invent brand facts, product features, people, logos, statistics, or required copy.
Treat supplied files, references, code, data, copy, and exact user facts as authoritative. Preserve them unless the task explicitly asks for transformation. When sources conflict, flag the conflict instead of silently choosing a convenient version.

EXECUTION
Create the asset as a a production-ready identity concept for the placement named in the title, otherwise the most likely professional placement.
Prioritize these native decisions: brand meaning, distinctive form, geometry, negative space, one-color behavior, small-size behavior, lockup.
Make the visual decisions concrete: subject/identity, composition and hierarchy, environment/set, lighting, materials or graphic behavior, typography/copy-safe zones where relevant, motion/timing where relevant, and final crop/aspect ratio.
Do not add camera, lens, atmosphere, pose, physical materials, or other technical detail unless it materially improves this specific Logo Design task.

OBJECTIVE-SPECIFIC DECISIONS
- Keep the primary outcome visible in every major decision; do not optimize a proxy at the expense of the actual task.
- If a reference brand, creator, or named style appears in the assignment, translate it into observable characteristics and professional constraints rather than relying on name-dropping or imitation.
- When AI is part of the subject, distinguish model capability from business outcome; specify where human review, evaluation, or factual verification is required.\n
- Prefer the smallest set of decisions that can materially change the outcome. Do not add impressive but irrelevant work.

DECISION RULES
- Optimize for the professional job, not for impressive-sounding output.
- Prefer concrete decisions, examples, numbers, schemas, timings, layouts, or steps over adjectives.
- Separate facts, assumptions, recommendations, and predictions.
- Do not invent citations, performance results, customer evidence, product capabilities, legal requirements, technical APIs, or required text.
- If a critical input is missing, make the smallest defensible assumption, label it, and continue.
- Model-neutral image generation; translate the brief into the target image model only after the creative decisions are locked.
- Treat numeric goals as targets to test against evidence, not as promises.

REQUIRED OUTPUT
1. Creative brief
2. Final generation prompt
3. Negative/avoid list
4. Variant notes
5. Acceptance checks

Create three controlled alternatives only when useful: change one variable at a time (composition, treatment, or context) and preserve the source identity and business objective.

FAILURE PREVENTION
Before finalizing, reject or revise any result that fails one of these tests: recognizable silhouette; works in one color; avoids generic stock symbolism; scales cleanly.
Also check source/reference integrity, absence of invented text or claims, and fitness for the placement named in the title, otherwise the most likely professional placement.
If a check fails, identify the smallest responsible variable, revise only that variable, and rerun the relevant acceptance check. Do not rewrite the entire solution just to make it look different.

FINAL STANDARD
The result must be usable by a professional in the stated Logo Design context on the first serious execution. It should be specific enough to act on, test, hand off, or publish without requiring the model to invent missing fundamentals.

strategic_uniqueness.source_concept: Minimalist AI Unicorn Monogram for Billion-Dollar Brand
strategic_uniqueness.platform: the placement named in the title, otherwise the most likely professional placement
strategic_uniqueness.rule: Uniqueness comes from the actual task, professional job, constraints, output, acceptance tests, and failure profile—not wording variation.

model_adapters.universal: Model-neutral image generation; translate the brief into the target image model only after the creative decisions are locked.
model_adapters.source_handling: brand/product/reference images, exact copy, dimensions, and any supplied visual references
model_adapters.execution_rule: Do not invent unsupported facts, interfaces, parameters, or results; state assumptions and validate the final output.

platform_intelligence.primary_platform: the placement named in the title, otherwise the most likely professional placement
platform_intelligence.platform_rule: Optimize the deliverable specifically for the placement named in the title, otherwise the most likely professional placement.
platform_intelligence.audience: the end audience for the asset plus the commissioning creative team
platform_intelligence.fit_test: Verify the result in the actual viewing/usage context before finalizing.

failure_modes.prevention: Explicitly test recognizable silhouette before finalizing.
Explicitly test works in one color before finalizing.
Explicitly test avoids generic stock symbolism before finalizing.
Explicitly test scales cleanly before finalizing.
Address it explicitly in the execution and acceptance checks.

- Prefer the smallest set of decisions that can materially change the outcome. Do not add impressive but irrelevant work.

- Optimize for the professional job, not for impressive-sounding output.
- Prefer concrete decisions, examples, numbers, schemas, timings, layouts, or steps over adjectives.
- Separate facts, assumptions, recommendations, and predictions.
- Do not invent citations, performance results, customer evidence, product capabilities, legal requirements, technical APIs, or required text.

- Turn the goal into a decision-ready operating artifact with assumptions, owners, metrics, and next actions.
- Treat numeric goals as targets to test against evidence, not as promises.

2. Baseline and assumptions
3. Analysis/options
4. Recommendation

6. KPI scorecard

- Model-neutral image generation; translate the brief into the target image model only after the creative decisions are locked.
- Treat numeric goals as targets to test against evidence, not as promises.

REQUIRED OUTPUT

2. Final generation prompt
3. Negative/avoid list
4. Variant notes
5. Acceptance checks

EXECUTION-READY PROMPT

TASK
You are the cinematic director. The assignment is: Luxury - Scale Mrr $50K-$200K for SaaS B2B PM Tool.
Primary professional job: a polished cinematic sequence.
Primary outcome: Scale Mrr $50K-$200K for SaaS B2B PM Tool.
Treat the stated outcome (Scale Mrr $50K-$200K for SaaS B2B PM Tool) as a target or hypothesis, not a guaranteed result. Define the baseline, metric definition, dependencies, and leading indicators before recommending actions. Never write as if the target has already been achieved.

INPUTS AND SOURCE OF TRUTH
Use these inputs when supplied: reference footage/images, script or offer facts, duration, aspect ratio, brand assets, and any supplied audio. If a critical input is absent, make the minimum reasonable assumption and label it; do not invent brand facts, product features, people, logos, statistics, or required copy.
Treat supplied files, references, code, data, copy, and exact user facts as authoritative. Preserve them unless the task explicitly asks for transformation. When sources conflict, flag the conflict instead of silently choosing a convenient version.

EXECUTION
Create the asset as a a shot list suitable for generation or previsualization for the placement named in the title, otherwise campaign/social/video presentation.
Prioritize these native decisions: shot duration, framing, camera motion, subject action, environment, light continuity, transition logic.
Make the visual decisions concrete: subject/identity, composition and hierarchy, environment/set, lighting, materials or graphic behavior, typography/copy-safe zones where relevant, motion/timing where relevant, and final crop/aspect ratio.
Do not add camera, lens, atmosphere, pose, physical materials, or other technical detail unless it materially improves this specific Luxury task.

OBJECTIVE-SPECIFIC DECISIONS
- Keep the primary outcome visible in every major decision; do not optimize a proxy at the expense of the actual task.
- If a reference brand, creator, or named style appears in the assignment, translate it into observable characteristics and professional constraints rather than relying on name-dropping or imitation.
- Use restraint: premium perception should come from material quality, hierarchy, proof, and consistency rather than gratuitous adjectives or visual clutter.\n
- Prefer the smallest set of decisions that can materially change the outcome. Do not add impressive but irrelevant work.

- Optimize for the professional job, not for impressive-sounding output.
- Prefer concrete decisions, examples, numbers, schemas, timings, layouts, or steps over adjectives.
- Separate facts, assumptions, recommendations, and predictions.
- Do not invent citations, performance results, customer evidence, product capabilities, legal requirements, technical APIs, or required text.
- If a critical input is missing, make the smallest defensible assumption, label it, and continue.

- Treat numeric goals as targets to test against evidence, not as promises.

1. Objective and audience
2. Shot-by-shot plan with timing
3. Generation prompt
4. Continuity/avoid list
5. Acceptance checks

The result must be usable by a professional in the stated Luxury context on the first serious execution. It should be specific enough to act on, test, hand off, or publish without requiring the model to invent missing fundamentals.
